— Driving, right of way and sharing rules","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Driving, right of way and sharing rules

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
Match speed to conditions, share the road courteously, and move only when safe and clear of traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
Walk around a parked car before reversing, and never reverse or halt in a travel lane; keep going to a safe pull-off. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
Obey officers, flaggers, traffic devices and traffic laws as the first rule of the road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A01
Signal one hundred feet before turning in town and three hundred feet before turning on rural roads. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A01
Keep right except to pass on roads with three or more same-direction lanes, favoring the center lane amid entering traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A01
After a missed turn or forgotten signal, continue to the next intersection, get in position, signal, then turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A01
Never drive on the shoulder unless directed to do so. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A02
Obey posted limits and drop below them for bad road or weather conditions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A02
Interstates post seventy-five or eighty for cars and light trucks by day and night, with heavy trucks held to sixty-five. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A02
Urban-area highways post sixty-five for all listed vehicles day and night near Billings, Great Falls and Missoula. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A02
Two-lane highways post seventy by day and sixty-five at night for cars and light trucks, with heavy trucks at sixty days and fifty-five nights. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A02
A two-lane driver may exceed the limit by ten miles per hour while overtaking and returning safely right. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A02
Pass only when safe, using the left of the centerline on two-lane roads and the leftmost lane on multi-lane roads. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A02
Passing on the right is legal only past a left-turning vehicle or on wide multi-lane pavement, never off the roadway or on the shoulder. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A02
Without turn controls, turn from the lane nearest the destination side into the nearest lane of the new road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A02
Keep right turns tight without swinging wide left first or finishing wide in the far lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A02
Avoid cutting left turns into approaching traffic while leaving room for oncoming left-turning vehicles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A03
Turn around only with five hundred feet of clear view both ways and no approaching vehicles, never on busy streets, curves or hills. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A03
No turn is made unless the vehicle is in the proper lane and the move is safe. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A03
The law assigns yielding duty and grants no absolute right-of-way, so every driver must act to avoid striking anyone. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A03
Blind pedestrians with a guide dog or white cane hold absolute right-of-way; never sound the horn at them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A03
Drivers yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, yet no pedestrian may step off the curb into a vehicle path. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A03
Night walkers should wear light clothing or carry a light, and walking on the roadway is unlawful where sidewalks exist. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A03
Roadway walkers keep left facing traffic, cross at intersections using provided crosswalks, and obey applicable traffic laws. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A04
Drivers crossing sidewalks or entering and leaving driveways, alleys and lots yield to pedestrians; sidewalk driving is illegal except to cross. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A04
Left-turning drivers yield to oncoming through traffic, and circle entrants yield to traffic already circulating. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A04
At uncontrolled intersections yield to the vehicle on the right, staying ready to yield by covering the brake and scanning both ways. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A04
At a four-way stop the first arrival goes first after a full stop; driveway and roadside entrants stop and yield to main-road traffic. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A04
Never enter an intersection without room to clear it, and treat a yield sign as an order to slow and yield to all vehicles. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F30 | anchor: A04
Right on red is allowed after stopping in the proper lane when safe unless signed otherwise, as is left on red between one-way streets. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F31 | anchor: A04
Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks; a stopped driver turns right only when the pedestrian is in the opposite half and safe. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F32 | anchor: A04
Drivers behind a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian must not pass the stopped vehicle. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F33 | anchor: A04
An overtaking driver yields to the vehicle being passed even as it slows or stops. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F34 | anchor: A04
Yield to siren-and-light emergency vehicles by pulling as far right as possible, obeying loudspeaker orders, and staying stopped until they pass. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F35 | anchor: A04
Stop at least thirty feet from a red-flashing school bus from either direction until the lights end, slowing with care for slowing or yellow-flashing buses. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F36 | anchor: A05
Slow down and watch for children near schools day and night, checking speed on every approach. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F37 | anchor: A06
A funeral procession means two or more vehicles with lead and escort units, one carrying remains, traveling in daylight hours. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F38 | anchor: A06
Drivers outside a funeral procession must yield to it and may not cut between moving procession vehicles unless police-authorized or driving an emergency vehicle, join to gain its right-of-way, pass it on the right on a multi-lane highway unless it occupies the farthest left lane, or enter an intersection on red unless doing so without crossing its path [A06].
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F39 | anchor: A06
The lead vehicle obeys intersection controls, after which followers may proceed through with reasonable care for others. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F40 | anchor: A06
Procession drivers follow closely, cap speed at fifty-five on fast highways and near the limit elsewhere, burn all lights, and flash signals together on first and last cars. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F41 | anchor: A06
Procession drivers still yield to signaled emergency vehicles and keep due regard for every road user. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-F42 | anchor: A06
Bicycles count as vehicles under the traffic laws that reasonably fit, so motorists adjust for their slower travel when passing and sharing. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0052]

Misconceptions: The right-of-way is yielded, never taken; a bus on a separate road or sealed loading zone needs no stop.
Mnemonics: Authored cue: signal early, yield always, clear the box, guard the walker.
Glossary: Right-of-way; four-way stop; funeral procession; lead vehicle; escort vehicle; sharrow.
Dynamic facts: Posted limits, local U-turn bans and procession routes vary; obey the displayed control and local ordinance.
